1.outline: Term theme: 'Spreadsheet Modelling Pro'. Extend IF to nested IF for problems with more than two outcomes.
1.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, nested-IF reference.
objectives: Write a basic IF formula.
Extend it to a nested IF with three outcomes.
Test all three outcomes with sample data.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Beyond two outcomes
plan.detail: Recap IF, then show a grade-band problem needing more than two outcomes.

plan.title: Build a nested IF
plan.detail: Write =IF(B2>=80,"A",IF(B2>=60,"B","C")) and test with three score ranges.

plan.title: Boundary testing
plan.detail: Test scores of 59, 60, 79, 80 specifically — boundaries are where bugs hide. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working nested IF formula.
My formula correctly handles all three outcomes.
I tested boundary values specifically.

2.outline: Learn COUNTIF to count matching records and SUMIF to total matching values, both filtered by a condition.
2.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, COUNTIF/SUMIF reference.
objectives: Write a COUNTIF formula to count matches.
Write a SUMIF formula to total matches.
Explain the difference between COUNTIF and SUMIF.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Count vs total
plan.detail: Explain: COUNTIF counts how many, SUMIF adds up values, both filtered by a condition.

plan.title: Build both
plan.detail: Write =COUNTIF(range,"criteria") and =SUMIF(range,"criteria",sum_range) on sample data.

plan.title: Check against a manual count
plan.detail: Manually count a small subset to verify the formula result matches. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working COUNTIF formula.
I wrote a working SUMIF formula.
I can explain the difference between them.

3.outline: Learn a lookup function (VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH) to find a value in a table based on a key.
3.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, lookup reference.
objectives: Explain what a lookup does.
Write a working lookup formula.
Fix a lookup formula that returns an error.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What a lookup does
plan.detail: Real-world analogy: looking up a name in a phone book to find a number.

plan.title: Build a lookup
plan.detail: Write a lookup formula that finds a price or grade from a code, on a sample product/price table.

plan.title: Fix the error
plan.detail: Given a lookup formula with a deliberate mistake, find and fix it. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can explain what a lookup does in my own words.
I wrote a working lookup formula.
I fixed a broken lookup formula.

4.outline: Recap absolute references, then learn named ranges so formulas can refer to a range by a readable name instead of cell coordinates.
4.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, named-ranges reference.
objectives: Recap when to use an absolute reference.
Create a named range.
Use a named range inside a formula.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Absolute refs recap
plan.detail: Quick recap from Year 6/7: $ signs lock a reference when copying.

plan.title: Named ranges
plan.detail: Name a range (e.g. TaxRate) and use it in a formula instead of a cell reference.

plan.title: Readability check
plan.detail: Compare a formula with named ranges to one without — which is easier to read? Save and log out.

activities: Create and use a named range
successCriteria: I can explain when to use an absolute reference.
I created a named range.
I used a named range inside a formula.

5.outline: Start building a small simulation model — for example a simple game of chance or a savings-growth model — using this term's formulas.
5.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, model exemplar.
objectives: Plan a simulation model.
Set up inputs and formulas using IF, lookups or named ranges.
Check the model calculates sensibly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choose a simulation
plan.detail: Choose a simple simulation idea and sketch what inputs and formulas it needs.

plan.title: Build it
plan.detail: Set up inputs and formulas — using IF, a lookup, or a named range — to model the chosen scenario.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My model has clearly labelled inputs.
My model uses at least one of this term's formulas correctly.
My model calculates sensible results.

6.outline: Add a small dashboard of charts that summarise the model's results at a glance.
6.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, dashboard exemplar.
objectives: Choose charts that summarise the model well.
Arrange charts into a simple dashboard layout.
Check the dashboard is clear without extra explanation.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add summary charts
plan.detail: Add one or two charts that summarise the model's key results.

plan.title: Arrange the dashboard
plan.detail: Arrange charts and key numbers together on one view, titled clearly.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My dashboard has at least one summary chart.
My dashboard is arranged clearly on one view.
My dashboard is understandable without extra explanation.

7.outline: Write a short explanation of what the model and dashboard show, and what decision it might support.
7.sowResources: Microsoft Word / Google Docs, writing frame.
objectives: Interpret the model's key results.
Write a clear explanation for a non-technical reader.
Suggest one decision the results might support.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Explain to a non-expert
plan.detail: Discuss: how would you explain this model to someone who has never seen it?

plan.title: Write it up
plan.detail: Write a short, clear explanation of the results and a suggested decision.

plan.title: Peer check
plan.detail: Partner checks the explanation matches the actual dashboard. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My explanation is clear to a non-technical reader.
My explanation matches my actual results.
I suggested one decision the results support.

8.outline: Finish and polish the portfolio piece: a model using IF and a lookup or COUNTIF, presented with a dashboard chart.
8.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, portfolio folder.
objectives: Finish the model with IF and a lookup or COUNTIF.
Ensure the dashboard and write-up are complete.
Save the finished piece to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Finish the model
plan.detail: Complete the model, dashboard and write-up, ensuring at least IF plus one of lookup/COUNTIF are present.

plan.title: Rubric self-check
plan.detail: Check against the assessment rubric before saving.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: My model uses IF and a lookup or COUNTIF.
My model has a dashboard chart and write-up.
My finished model is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Return to the model and tidy it: replace loose cell references with named ranges and check formatting is consistent.
objectives: Replace at least one cell reference with a named range.
Check formatting is consistent throughout.
Re-test the model still calculates correctly.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Tidy the model
plan.detail: Add named ranges where useful and tidy up formatting inconsistencies.

plan.title: Re-test
plan.detail: Re-check every formula still calculates correctly after the changes.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: I replaced at least one reference with a named range.
My model's formatting is consistent.
My model still calculates correctly after tidying.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's modelling skills in pairs: nested IF, COUNTIF/SUMIF, a lookup, a dashboard chart.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's modelling skills in order.
Rehearse building a formula-driven model with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: nested IF, COUNTIF/SUMIF, lookup, dashboard — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build a small model with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's modelling skills in order.
I rehearsed the practical task with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: build a model using IF and a lookup or COUNTIF, presented with a dashboard chart.
objectives: Use nested IF, and a lookup or COUNTIF/SUMIF, correctly.
Use absolute references and/or named ranges appropriately.
Build and interpret a dashboard chart.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the model
plan.detail: Individual practical: apply this term's formulas to a given dataset.

plan.title: Dashboard and write-up
plan.detail: Add a dashboard chart and a one-sentence interpretation.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Save and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: My model uses nested IF correctly.
My model uses a lookup or COUNTIF/SUMIF correctly.
My dashboard chart is clear and interpreted.
